page: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an entry-tier offering in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, built on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction flags such as AES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and AVX. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB total (4.0 GB per vCPU), establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Local persistence is supplied via a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal pronounced single-threaded efficiency alongside expected constraints in multi-core scalability. The instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng (3135.87) and strong Geekbench single-core output (2117.0), complemented by solid text processing performance (2605.0). However, the two-thread hardware profile restricts aggregate multithreaded capacity, yielding below-average multi-core scores in both Geekbench (3796.0) and PassMark (5488.88). Memory operations reflect moderate large-block bandwidth (71.86 GB/s read and 53.72 GB/s write), while cached small-block bandwidth remains modest. PassMark database tests and static web serving throughput show lower-tier results, reflecting the bounded processing capacity of a dual-thread configuration.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the dedicated vCPU allocation ensures reliable execution free from noisy-neighbor CPU throttling, providing a stable footprint for smaller persistent workloads. The absence of an accelerator and the compact 50 GB NVMe drive rule out large-scale data science pipelines, dense relational databases, or heavy parallel compilation. Instead, the server provides an optimal profile for lightweight web services, small automation workers, API backends, development or staging environments, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks.
description: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute series, provisioned with 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical AMD EPYC core running at 2.0 GHz. The instance supplies 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and one public IPv4 address. Single-threaded performance is a notable asset, marked by a top-tier stress-ng single-core rating and strong Geekbench single-core and text processing scores. Conversely, overall multi-core throughput and database execution remain limited due to the two-thread ceiling. With no discrete GPU acceleration and constrained aggregate parallel bandwidth, this instance presents a balanced, cost-effective profile for moderately demanding tasks. It is well configured for lightweight application serving, background script execution, staging environments, API gateways, and light web or text-processing utilities.
